definitions.gloss: scripture; sacred text; sutra; canonical text
definitions.explanation: A religious text that is considered authoritative and sacred, especially Buddhist sutras. Can also refer to the sacred writings of other religions.

examples.japanese: {僧侶|そうりょ}が{経典|きょうてん}を{唱|とな}えている。
examples.english: The monk is chanting from the scriptures.

examples.japanese: この{寺|てら}には{古|ふる}い{経典|きょうてん}が{数多|かずおお}く{保管|ほかん}されている。
examples.english: This temple houses a great many ancient scriptures.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}の{経典|きょうてん}はサンスクリット{語|ご}から{漢訳|かんやく}されたものが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many Buddhist scriptures were translated into Chinese from Sanskrit.

notes:
Composed of {経|きょう} (sutra, scripture) and {典|てん} (code, canon, authoritative text). While it can refer to the sacred texts of any religion, it is most commonly used in Buddhist contexts in Japanese.

In Buddhism, the {経典|きょうてん} include the vast body of sutras ({経|きょう}), monastic rules ({律|りつ}), and commentaries ({論|ろん}), collectively known as the {三蔵|さんぞう} (Tripitaka). Many of these texts reached Japan via Chinese translation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経典|きょうてん}を{読|よ}む: to read the scriptures
- {経典|きょうてん}を{唱|とな}える: to chant the scriptures
- {仏教|ぶっきょう}{経典|きょうてん}: Buddhist scripture
- {経典|きょうてん}の{研究|けんきゅう}: study of scriptures

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{経|きょう}: sutra, Buddhist chanting — more colloquial and everyday; often refers to the act of chanting rather than the text itself
- {聖典|せいてん}: sacred scripture, holy text — a broader term applicable to any religion; {経典|きょうてん} leans toward Buddhist texts specifically
- {聖書|せいしょ}: the Bible — specifically the Christian scriptures
